specific_competences.main_competence: Demonstrate mastery of basic concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
specific_competences.specific_competence: Demonstrate mastery of concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
learning_activities: (a) Describe the concept of Chemistry (meaning, branches, applications and relationships with other disciplines)
(b) Discuss the contribution of Chemistry in the development of modern society
(c) Describe the concept of matter (physical and chemical changes of matter)
(d) Describe the concepts of chemical elements (criteria for assigning chemical symbols), compounds (binary compound) and mixtures (types of solution and separation of mixtures)
(e) Compare the properties of compounds with those of constituent elements
(f) Explain the concept of the periodic table (1st 20 elements in the Periodic Table; metals and non- metals)
teaching_methods: Brainstorming: Assign students in manageable groups to brainstorm on chemical basis of materials from their environment, give the meaning of Chemistry and justifying the reason for studying Chemistry Project works: Guide students to explore the common industrial products in Tanzania and relate their applications to the importance of Chemistry
Field visit: Guide students to visit any nearby industry, health facilities, mining sites and agricultural farms to appreciate the importance of Chemistry in the development of societies

Practical work: Guide students to carry-out hands- on activities to investigate the physical and chemical changes of matter using samples of substances found in their environment Experimentation: Guide students to perform experiments basing on sublimation of compounds, rusting of iron nails, freezing and evaporation of water and dissolving of salts using distilled water

Think-ink-pair-share: Guide students in pairs to think and share about various types of industrial products they commonly use in their home for various activities, reflect on their constituent elements and explain the meaning of element, compound and mixture Hands-on-minds-on: Assign students to prepare solutions using materials available in their home settings and reflect their properties to practices of using them in various applications such as pharmaceuticals and domestic activities

Group discussion: Guide students in manageable groups to explore the properties of chemical compounds useful in real-life situation Technological -based learning: Guide students to analyse features of compounds and element from real substances using visual aids

Outdoor activity: Assign students to collect materials in their environment and classify into metals and non-metals Project works: Assign students to carry-out project task to investigate on different properties of metals and non-metals available in their real life setting and write a report
assessment_criteria: The concept of Chemistry is clearly described
The contribution of Chemistry in the development of modern society is clearly recognised
The concept of matter is clearly described
The concepts of chemical elements, compounds and mixture are clearly described
The properties of compounds are correctly compared with those of constituent elements
The concept of the periodic table is clearly explained
resources: Pictures, diagrams, simulations, animations or videos illustrating the meaning, branches, applications and relationship with other disciplines
Simulations, animations or videos illustrating the contribution of Chemistry in the development of modern society

learning_activities: (a) Describe basic Chemistry laboratory skills (chemistry laboratory rules and safety measures, first aid, fire and firefighting, and Chemistry laboratory apparatus)
(b) Perform experiments on the changes of matter from one state to another
(c) Perform experiments on separation of different mixtures using different methods
teaching_methods: Group discussion: Guide students in manageable groups to interpret basic laboratory skills related to rules and precautions, safety measures and chemical warning signs Guest speaker from fire brigade: Guide students to interpret classes of fire and practice on firefighting basing on speaker’s instructions and write a report Outdoor activity: Guide students to practice on extinguishing small fires
Experimentation: Guide students to perform experiments on various materials from the environment and laboratory, and use chemicals to demonstrate changes of matter

Home-based project: Assign students to carry- out simple experiments on separating mixtures in their daily life Experimentation: Guide students to perform experiments on separating mixtures basing on specific properties of substances such as solubility and boiling point Questions and answers: Guide students to present the common and commercial applications of the various methods for separating mixtures, for examples simple distillation, fractional distillation and decantation
assessment_criteria: Basic Chemistry laboratory skills are clearly described
Experiments on the changes of matter from one state to another are correctly performed
Experiments on separation of different mixtures using different methods are correctly performed
resources: Laboratory manuals, models, pictures, wall charts with written laboratory rules, first aid kit, laboratory apparatus, fire extinguishers and videos illustrating basic chemistry laboratory skills

specific_competences.main_competence: Demonstrate mastery of basic concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
specific_competences.specific_competence: Demonstrate mastery of concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
learning_activities: (a) Describe the modern concept of atomic structure (Dalton’s atomic structure and sub- atomic particles)
(b) Describe the concept of electronic arrangements
(c) Use the concept of atomic structure to determine the atomic and mass numbers of an element
(d) Explain the concept of chemical formulae and nomenclature (valence, oxidation state, radicals and naming of binary inorganic compounds using the IUPAC system)
(e) Determine empirical and molecular formulae of common compounds
(f) Describe the concept of chemical bonding (covalent and electrovalent bonding)
(g) Describe the concept of chemical reactions (chemical equations, balancing chemical equations, and types of chemical reactions)
(h) Relate the types of chemical reactions with common processes in daily life such as burning of fuel and digestion in living organisms
(i) Describe acids, bases and salts (reactions of acids and bases with various substances) and their applications in daily life
teaching_methods: Think-ink-pair- share: Guide students in pair to think about the meaning of an atom and its structure Technological-based learning: Guide students to account for the structure of an atom basing on ICT facilities and write a report

Technological- based learning: Guide students to watch visual aids for simulations and animations, showing the arrangements of electrons in atoms of elements in their shells and write a report Group activity: Assign students in manageable groups to practice the arrangement of electrons in shells of atoms of different elements through models designing using locally available materials
Group discussion: Guide students in manageable groups to calculate the atomic number and mass number of an element for the given compound

Inquiry-based learning: Assign students to collect commonly used substances and give their common names and identify their constituent elements Group discussion: Guide student in manageable groups to describe the concepts of chemical formula, valence, oxidation state, radicals and name binary inorganic compounds using the IUPAC system Gallery work: Guide students to brainstorm and share key rules in writing chemical formulae

Group discussion: Guide students in manageable groups to determine percentage compositions of each element and in a compound Problem solving: Guide students to apply steps for calculating empirical formulae and molecular formulae of different compounds

Outdoor activity: Guide students to reflect on real-environment about bonding such as building blocks erecting a walls and relate with the concepts of bonding Technological-based learning: Use software such as ChemDraw to demonstrate the process of bonding

Group discussion: Guide students in manageable groups to write simple word equations and chemical equations with symbols Think-ink-pair-share: Guide students in pairs to identify types of chemical reactions, balance chemical equations, interpret word equations into chemical equations Experimentation: Guide students to perform an experiment to verify the law of conservation of matter and write the report
Project works: Task students to carry-out project to examine applications of chemical reactions in the burning of fuel and digestion in living organisms

Inquiry-based learning: Guide students to analyse various substances with acidic and basic properties commonly found in their environment and describe the concepts of acids, bases and salts Group discussion: Guide students in manageable groups to describe the reactions of acids and bases Field trips: Guide students to visit nearby food and beverages processing industries to examine the applications of acids, bases and salts
assessment_criteria: The modern concept of atomic structure is clearly described
The concept of electronic arrangements in atoms is clearly described
Atomic numbers and mass numbers of elements are correctly determined
The concept of chemical formulae and nomenclature are clearly explained
Empirical formulae and molecular formulae of different compounds are correctly determined
The concept of chemical bonding is clearly described
The concept of chemical reactions is clearly described
The types of chemical reactions are clearly related with common processes in daily life
The concepts of acids, bases and salts are clearly described

learning_activities: (a) Describe the mole concept (comparison of the mole with other units of measurements and molar quantities of substances)
(b) Explain Avogadro’s law in relation to molar quantities
(c) Explain the principles of volumetric analysis (preparation of standard solutions and volumetric calculations)
(d) Describe the applications of volumetric analysis in real life and industrial settings as in soft drinks and cocktail making, medicine and in agriculture
(e) Explore the basic tenets of ionic theory and electrolysis (ionic theory, mechanism of electrolysis and laws of electrolysis)
(f) Describe the preparation and properties of various compounds of metals (oxides, hydroxides, carbonates, hydrogen carbonates, nitrates, chlorides and sulphates of metals)
(g) Describe the oxidizing and displacement properties of non-metal compounds (oxygen, hydrogen, chlorine, hydrogen chloride, sulphur dioxide, nitrogen, ammonia, and carbon dioxide)
teaching_methods: Outdoor learning: Assign students to visit nearby shops to explore items that are sold in units such as water in catorns, pair of shoes and other quantities and describe the concept of mole and molar quantities of substances Classroom assignments: Assign students to work on calculations and conversions of masses and volumes of substances to moles and vice versa
Group discussion: Guide student in manageable groups to use the Avogadros Law in explaining the molar quantities

Brainstorming: Assign students to brainstorm on the concept of volumetric analysis Project works: Guide students to carry-out a visit to nearby possible industries eg. Foods, drinks, cosmetics and pharmaceuticals industries to analyse procedures for determining amounts of chemical substances. Group discussion: Guide students in manageable groups to perform volumetric calculations and make classroom presentations
Experimentation: Guide students to perform experiments related to the applications of volumetric analysis

Group discussion: Guide students in manageable groups to describe the concept of ionic theory and electrolysis and make presentations Experimentation: Guide students to carry-out experiments that demonstrate the mechanism of electrolysis using simple available chemicals and apparatus Field Trip: Guide students to carry-out fields trips to near by industries involved in extraction, electroplating and purification of metals and examine the applications of electrolysis
Inquiry-based learning: Guide students to investigate properties of compound of metals and relate with extraction of metals, making of paints, textiles, drinking water, soaps, and detergents

Group discussion: Guide students in manageable groups to describe the properties of non-metals and write report Project works: Guide students to carry- out visits to nearby industries for making gases, pesticides, fertilisers and other chemicals, analyse properties of the compounds of non- metals

The applications of volumetric analysis in real life and industrial settings are clearly described
The basic principles of ionic theory and electrolysis are clearly described
The preparation and properties of various compounds of metals are clearly described
Oxidizing and displacement properties of non-metal compounds are clearly described
